_readme: The tracks: the licensed greyhound tracks racing in Britain in 2026, by place name. Distances and race days come from public sources; circumferences are real where known and estimated otherwise. Every track is an oval: two straights joined by two half-circle bends, run anticlockwise. place = where it is. straight = length of each straight in metres. radius = radius of the bends in metres (smaller is tighter). finishBeforeBend = how far the finish line is before bend 1. distances = the race distances this track stages, in metres, by kind of race: sprint (D grades), standard (A grades), middle (B grades, a second standard trip), stay (S grades), marathon (M grades) and hurdle (H grades, over hurdles). Leave a kind out and the track doesn't stage those races. Every track needs a standard distance. nights = the days of the week the track races (Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun). goingBase = how slow the sand usually rides (0 is normal, + is slower, - is faster; a day's going is this plus a random amount). stands = the grandstands along the home straight, in order, repeated along the track (names from "stands" in assets/manifest.json: standard_a, standard_b, heritage, premium, terrace, pavilion, tournament, sponsors, and each track's own section with its name board, such as rail_centralpark). On competition nights the tournament stand is added too. Add a track by copying a whole { ... } block. The id must be unique and have no spaces.

tracks.name: Central Park
tracks.description: Relaid in 2023 with new distances; a fair, galloping circuit.

tracks.name: Doncaster
tracks.description: A big track near Doncaster with two standard trips.

tracks.name: Dunstall Park
tracks.description: The newest track, opened in 2025 inside Wolverhampton Racecourse. Wide and galloping.

tracks.name: Harlow
tracks.description: A compact Essex track that stages hurdles over its standard trip.

tracks.name: Brighton & Hove
tracks.description: A fair, galloping track with banked bends; dogs coming from behind do well.

tracks.name: Kinsley
tracks.description: A small Yorkshire track that began life as a flapping track in 1939.

tracks.name: Monmore
tracks.description: Busy Midlands track with well-banked bends and a true surface.

tracks.name: Newcastle
tracks.description: A fast surface that produces quick times.

tracks.name: Nottingham
tracks.description: A big galloping track with long straights and wide, sweeping bends.

tracks.name: Oxford
tracks.description: Sandy Lane, back racing since 2022; the back straight runs beside the railway.

tracks.name: Romford
tracks.description: Small and tight with sharp bends: early pace and an inside draw are a big help.

tracks.name: Sheffield
tracks.description: Owlerton: an all-sand oval shared with speedway, with hurdles over 500m.

tracks.name: Star Pelaw
tracks.description: The smallest track of all, formerly Pelaw Grange. Hurdle racing returned in 2026.

tracks.name: Sunderland
tracks.description: A steady, workmanlike track with a well-kept surface.

tracks.name: Towcester
tracks.description: Home of the Derby: very wide bends and long straights inside the racecourse.

tracks.name: The Valley
tracks.description: The only track in Wales, beside the Rhymney River.

tracks.name: Yarmouth
tracks.description: East Anglia's track, home of the East Anglian Derby; the sea air can slow the times.
